Pilot preparation of InVEST climate parameters

11 November 2026 · v5 diagnostic pilot · Copy-friendly HTML

Retained manuscript configuration

Author decision, 11 November 2026: retain T_ref = 25°C and UHI_max = 5°C for the prescribed 2050 scenario, and retain 28/5°C for the prescribed 2070 scenario. Existing production outputs remain the manuscript basis. Report this as a prescribed warm-condition stress-test, not an observationally calibrated 2050 or 2070 daily-maximum climate estimate. Retain the temperature-only 2/3/5°C comparison as supporting sensitivity evidence; it establishes ranking stability within this model, not robustness of downstream health or work-capacity magnitudes. No further production reruns are required by this decision, and health/work-capacity sensitivity tests remain on hold. Additional station calibration is a future improvement, not a prerequisite for this retained prescribed-condition analysis. Copy-ready Methods and Figure 3 legend/Results are maintained in the Figure 3 review document, not duplicated here.

Evidence and qualification

Retain 25/5°C only as an explicitly prescribed warm stress-test, not as a calibrated 2050 climate estimate. The future-temperature pilot supports a reference temperature close to 25°C in 2050. The expanded 10-station, six-July pilot does not support 5°C as a representative July daily-maximum air-temperature contrast. A stricter exposure screen leaves only one urban-background station; against three rural-background stations, its daily-maximum P90 is 1.38°C, while the hot-day night-time P90 is 4.97°C. Thus 5°C is defensible only as an upper-tail nocturnal or prescribed stress-test, not as the representative daily-maximum contrast paired with July T_ref. The screened result is diagnostic rather than a replacement production parameter. A temperature-only sensitivity at T_ref = 25°C shows that the ranking of the nine land-use scenarios is identical at UHI_max = 2, 3 and 5°C; the parameter mainly scales absolute temperature effects. Health and work-capacity testing remains on hold. An independent Crowd-Grid spatial sensitivity reaches the same conclusion: the robust July daily-maximum contrast never reaches 5°C, whereas the hot-day daily-minimum P90 is 5.08°C.

Pilot design

The pilot used the four locally available MIDAS stations with complete July 2021 files: St James’s Park, Kew Gardens, Kenley Airfield and Battersea Heliport. Kenley was the provisional rural station because it is peripheral and its 500-m surroundings are 70.4% grass and 21.7% urban in LCM2023. It is 170 m above sea level, so its temperatures were also translated to a common 5-m elevation using a fixed 0.0065°C m⁻¹ lapse rate. This correction is a sensitivity assumption, not a substitute for low-elevation rural observations.

For each station, the analysis calculated July daily maxima from numeric hourly observations, requiring at least 18 observations per day. All 31 days passed at all four stations; hourly completeness was 99.6–100%. The provisional UHI was the 90th percentile of the daily difference between the warmest of the three urban candidates and elevation-adjusted Kenley.

The map shows why the result remains provisional: three stations are clustered in inner/west London, while the only peripheral candidate is Kenley. It is not a spatially balanced urban–rural monitoring network.

The future rural reference used the delta method:

observed Kenley reference + future WorldClim July Tmax − historical WorldClim July Tmax

at Kenley for ACCESS-CM2, IPSL-CM6A-LR and MRI-ESM2-0. SSP370 and SSP585 were kept separate for both 2041–2060 (2050) and 2061–2080 (2070). Five baseline-land-use, temperature-only InVEST 3.20.2 runs were then made: observed 2021 and the two SSPs in 2050 and 2070. No energy, health or work-capacity component was run.

The GCM-specific SSP370 reference temperatures range from 24.49 to 25.49°C; SSP585 ranges from 24.59 to 25.89°C. Thus the existing 25°C reference is close to this pilot’s mid-century rural-temperature estimate. The existing 5°C UHI, however, is above every observed July 2021 contrast in this four-station pilot. This does not establish that 5°C is impossible during other years, hours or heat events.

For 2070, the GCM-specific reference temperatures span 24.79–26.99°C under SSP370 and 25.29–27.59°C under SSP585. These ranges represent model spread, not a confidence interval.

Expanded six-year station check

The acquisition pilot adds five provisional urban and five provisional rural stations for July 2018–2023 (60 station-year files). MIDAS version-1 records were deduplicated by station and observation time, retaining the latest record timestamp. Primary estimates exclude temperatures whose MIDAS status digit is 1 (observed but suspect); status 0 denotes observed and not suspect. The interpretation follows the official MIDAS quick-start guide and quality-code table.

Daily extrema require at least 18 distinct hourly records. Daily maximum is the primary statistic because Figure 1 and T_ref use July maximum temperature. As a supplementary check using the same hourly MIDAS files, daytime means use 09:00–17:00 UTC (approximately 10:00–18:00 British Summer Time) and require at least seven of nine observations. Night-time means use 22:00–05:00 UTC and require at least six of eight observations. The daytime window is deliberately reported as a sensitivity rather than substituted for daily maximum: an average over daytime hours and the daily maximum are different estimands, but agreement between them helps show whether the result is driven by one extreme hour. The urban and rural daily values are medians across available stations, requiring at least three stations per group. “Hot days” are the 19 dates on or above the pooled 90th percentile of the rural-network July daily maximum. The fixed 0.0065°C m⁻¹ translation to 5 m is retained only as an elevation sensitivity.

All July days: daytime mean 0.46°C 1.04°C 2.13°C 0.26°C 0.82°C 1.98°C
All July days: night-time mean 1.38°C 2.95°C 3.86°C 1.16°C 2.80°C 3.56°C
Hot days: daily maximum 0.55°C 1.27°C 1.40°C 0.26°C 0.88°C 1.08°C

The result depends on the temperature statistic. Daily maximum and daytime mean give closely similar, modest contrasts; the nocturnal signal is larger and increases on hot days. This supports retaining daily maximum as the primary statistic, using daytime mean as corroboration, and treating daytime and night-time UHI as distinct quantities. Including suspect records raises the hot-day raw night-time median from 2.09°C to 2.70°C, but its maximum remains 3.85°C. Leave-one-station-out maxima reach 4.24°C for night-time means and 2.75°C for daily maxima. None of these checks validates 5°C as the representative July daily-maximum input used in the production run.

Station-history and exposure screen

The formal screen combines official MIDAS source and station-remark records, temperature QC, and ESA WorldCover 2021 built cover within 1 km. The diagnostic thresholds were specified before recalculating UHI: urban background requires at least 50% built cover; rural background requires at most 10% built cover and elevation no higher than 100 m. Intermediate sites are classified as transition/green-space settings. An official all-elements-suspect remark or at least 50% suspect temperature records overrides land-cover classification.

Only St James’s Park passes as an urban-background candidate (67.9% built cover within 1 km). Wisley, Charlwood and Woburn pass as rural-background candidates (6.5%, 2.3% and 1.1% built cover). Kew Gardens, Teddington–Bushy Park, Northolt, Writtle and East Malling lie between the pre-specified thresholds and are not used in the screened contrast. Battersea Heliport is rejected: all its numeric temperatures carry MIDAS status 1, and the official station remark states that all elements are suspect because of tall buildings, rotor wash, engine exhaust, heat sources and a non-standard screen.

This screen sharpens rather than reverses the interpretation. A 5°C contrast is plausible in the upper tail of hot-night conditions, but it remains unsupported for the July daily-maximum statistic paired with the current reference temperature. Because only one urban-background site passes, the screened result cannot support spatial calibration or held-out validation. Additional quality-controlled urban air-temperature stations are the limiting requirement.

Temperature-only UHI sensitivity

To determine whether the uncertain UHI_max changes the land-use conclusions, InVEST 3.20.2 was run at T_ref = 25°C with UHI_max = 2°C and 3°C for the baseline and all nine land-use scenarios. These diagnostic runs used the same land-cover rasters, biophysical table, evapotranspiration input, grid and model settings as the existing UHI_max = 5°C production run. Only temperature was calculated; energy, WBGT, health and the modified Hothaps work-capacity component were not run. The existing 5°C temperature rasters were reused rather than overwritten.

Scenario Cooling at UHI 2°C Cooling at UHI 3°C Cooling at UHI 5°C Rank at all settings
Target30 0.128°C 0.192°C 0.319°C 1
Green30 0.116°C 0.175°C 0.291°C 2
Target20 0.086°C 0.129°C 0.215°C 3
Green20 0.078°C 0.117°C 0.195°C 4
Target10 0.045°C 0.068°C 0.113°C 5
Green10 0.041°C 0.061°C 0.102°C 6
TreeOpp 0.025°C 0.037°C 0.062°C 7
TreeRisk −0.031°C −0.046°C −0.076°C 8
AllBuilt −0.444°C −0.665°C −1.109°C 9

Values are London-boundary, equal-cell-area means relative to the matching baseline; positive values indicate cooling and negative values warming. Scenario rankings are identical across all three UHI settings (Spearman rank correlation = 1.00 for every pair). Target produces slightly more London-wide cooling than Green within each matched canopy tier at every setting. At the 30% tier, the Target-minus-Green difference scales from 0.011°C at UHI 2°C to 0.017°C at UHI 3°C and 0.028°C at UHI 5°C. The borough direction is also stable: Target30 cools more than Green30 in 19 boroughs, while Green30 cools more in 14.

This is expected from the InVEST air-temperature equation: for fixed cooling coefficients, temperature differences scale approximately linearly with UHI_max. The sensitivity therefore supports the comparative conclusion that scenario ranking and the Green–Target contrast are robust to the tested UHI range. It does not validate 5°C as a representative daytime parameter, and absolute temperatures and downstream health or work-capacity magnitudes would change if a different UHI value were adopted.

Crowd-Grid spatial sensitivity

Crowd-Grid v1.0 was added as a complementary spatial check because the official MIDAS screen leaves only one eligible urban-background station. This Met Office prototype combines quality-controlled official, crowdsourced and roadside observations to estimate daily maximum and minimum air temperature at 1-km resolution. The Recent Heat Packs average those grids over local-authority and 2021 MSOA boundaries. Crowd-Grid is designed to represent built environments better than HadUK-Grid, but its uncertainty is larger because many observations come from non-standard exposures. It is therefore used here as a sensitivity, not as a new production parameter or a replacement for direct observations.

For each July day in 2018–2023, the robust spatial proxy is the 90th percentile across London MSOAs minus the median of the three MSOAs containing the screened rural MIDAS stations: Guildford 001 (Wisley), Crawley 001 (Charlwood) and Central Bedfordshire 007 (Woburn). The supplied 2021 boundary file, rather than an assumed district name, resolves these locations. “Hot days” are the 53 dates on which the London MSOA 90th percentile of daily maximum temperature reached at least 28°C. Because these are MSOA averages, the contrasts smooth local extremes.

Crowd-Grid contrast July days Median P90 Maximum Days at least 5°C
Daily maximum: London MSOA P90 − rural MSOA median 186 1.60°C 2.68°C 4.00°C 0.0%
Daily minimum: London MSOA P90 − rural MSOA median 186 2.50°C 4.50°C 5.80°C 5.9%
Hot-day daily maximum: London MSOA P90 − rural MSOA median 53 2.20°C 3.40°C 4.00°C 0.0%
Hot-day daily minimum: London MSOA P90 − rural MSOA median 53 4.00°C 5.08°C 5.30°C 15.1%

The result independently confirms the statistic-specific interpretation. A 5°C contrast is not representative of July daily maximum temperature: even the robust spatial maximum across 186 days is 4.00°C. It is, however, plausible in the upper tail of daily minimum temperature during hot conditions. A less robust maximum-London-MSOA comparison reaches 5.80°C by day and 6.60°C by night, but it is too sensitive to a single MSOA to define a production parameter. Crowd-Grid therefore strengthens the stress-test framing; it does not remove the need for additional well-exposed urban stations and held-out validation.

Source and interpretation follow the Crowd-Grid catalogue record and official README. The product is licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0 and must be cited using the catalogue citation.

Baseline model check

Against the four elevation-adjusted station means, the observed-period baseline run has bias = MAE = 0.80°C, RMSE = 0.97°C, and correlation = −0.54. The correlation is descriptive only (n = 4). Kenley is the coolest observed station but is the warmest modelled station among the four. An unconstrained two-parameter fit therefore returns a physically impossible negative UHI (−3.25°C). This is evidence that the available network and/or current model spatial coefficients cannot calibrate a defensible UHI—not evidence of a real negative London UHI.

Observed 2021 21.85 23.70 +1.85
SSP370 2041–2060 25.72 26.47 +0.75
SSP585 2041–2060 26.06 26.77 +0.71
SSP370 2061–2080 26.64 27.34 +0.70
SSP585 2061–2080 27.31 28.04 +0.72

These are not like-for-like validation statistics: Figure 1 is an equal-borough summary of gridded climate products, whereas the UCM value is an area-weighted mean that explicitly adds local urban heat. They are retained as a consistency check, not calibrated targets.

Data-quality findings

Finding Evidence and consequence Severity
Urban network is inadequate After official-history, QC and land-cover screening, only St James’s Park remains an urban-background candidate. This is insufficient for spatial calibration or held-out validation. High
Spatial validation fails Negative four-station correlation and physically impossible fitted UHI. Do not use the pilot parameters as production estimates. High
Temporal evidence is still limited Six Julys improve on the original single-year pilot, but do not establish long-term return levels or future UHI sensitivity. Medium
Crowd-Grid is a prototype spatial sensitivity The 1-km product improves built-environment coverage, but includes non-standard exposures and the Heat Packs spatially average grid cells over MSOAs. Use it to test the 5°C framing, not as a calibrated UHI_max. Medium
QC invalidates Battersea Code 106 marks observed-but-suspect data, and the official remark independently identifies site heat/exhaust/rotor effects. Battersea is excluded; some Kew records are also excluded. High
Future anomaly has limited spatial support It is sampled at Kenley only, although three GCMs and matched historical/future WorldClim data are used. Medium

Approaches for estimating London UHI

Different methods estimate different quantities. For this project, UHI_max must be a near-surface air-temperature contrast for the same period and temperature statistic as T_ref; a nocturnal extreme or satellite surface temperature should not silently replace a July daily-maximum air-temperature contrast.

Approach Contribution Recommended use here
Official urban–rural stations Traceable hourly air temperature and long records Primary estimate after expanding to several rural and urban sites and stratifying by hour, wind and hot days
Quality-controlled personal weather stations Dense intra-urban spatial coverage Secondary spatial calibration after radiation, siting, duplication and persistence checks
LCZ/land-use regression or GAM Converts observations into a spatial air-temperature field Fit canopy, built cover, elevation, distance and weather effects; validate on held-out stations
UKCP Local or WRF–SUEWS Weather-dependent and future urban-climate sensitivity Process-based sensitivity, not a substitute for observational calibration
Landsat/ECOSTRESS land-surface temperature Fine-scale hot-surface diagnosis Supporting spatial evidence only; do not use directly as UHI_max

London evidence supports separating ordinary and extreme conditions. A six-year, quality-controlled crowd-station study found a persistent Greater London air-temperature contrast of about 1.0–1.5°C, whereas summertime monitoring has reported occasional nocturnal intensity near 7°C. An older St James’s Park–Wisley analysis reported a mean nocturnal contrast of 1.8°C and values of at least 5°C on 5% of days. These values are not contradictory: they refer to different time windows, stations and statistics. They indicate that 5°C is plausible as an upper-tail nocturnal condition, but do not validate it as the July daily-maximum parameter used in this pilot.

The recommended workflow is therefore to estimate separate multi-year distributions for daytime maximum, nighttime minimum and hot-day conditions; fit an LCZ/land-cover model; validate it on held-out sites; and only then choose a pre-declared percentile matching the manuscript estimand.

The current MIDAS metadata screen found 52 stations within 100 km of central London that were active in 2021 and below 150 m elevation. This is an acquisition pool, not a rural classification. Plausible directions for manual exposure and file checks include Wisley or Charlwood to the south-west, Writtle to the north-east, East Malling to the south-east and Woburn or another comparable northern site.

Expanded station-pilot status

A balanced acquisition pilot has been prepared for six Julys (2018–2023):

Provisional group Stations
Urban candidates St James’s Park, Battersea Heliport, Kew Gardens, Teddington–Bushy Park, Northolt
Rural candidates Wisley, Charlwood, Writtle, East Malling, Woburn

All 60 expected station-year files were downloaded from MIDAS Open v202607 and verified against recorded SHA-256 hashes. Their exact URLs and provisional roles are recorded in climate/uhi_station_pilot_20261111_v1/midas_uhi_acquisition_manifest.csv. The station roles remain hypotheses until surrounding land cover, exposure and station histories are checked. The project-local token file was used only for authenticated acquisition, is ignored by Git and is owner-readable only. It should be deleted when the short-lived token expires. A future acquisition can be resumed with:

python3 code/preprocessing_layers/download_midas_uhi_pilot.py \
  "/path/to/Wellcome Trust Project Data/1_preprocess/UrbanCoolingModel/OfficialWorkingInputs/climate/uhi_station_pilot_20261111_v1" \
  --years 2018 2019 2020 2021 2022 2023 --resume \
  --token-file "/secure/local/path/to/CEDA_token.txt"

The downloader rejects token files readable by other users, never stores or prints the token, reports progress by station-year, validates each BADC-CSV, records SHA-256 hashes and resumes already validated files without overwriting them. Delete the local token file after downloading or when the short-lived token expires.

Required improvement before manuscript production runs

  1. Acquire additional quality-controlled urban-background air-temperature stations. The current official MIDAS pool provides only one defensible urban site after screening, so a held-out spatial model cannot yet be fitted.
  2. Extend the screened St James’s Park–rural comparison to at least ten recent Julys as a temporal sensitivity, retaining the explicit MIDAS QC rules and separate daytime, night-time and hot-day estimands. This does not replace the need for additional urban sites.
  3. Replace the fixed lapse correction with either comparable-elevation station selection or an empirically estimated elevation term.
  4. Recalculate rural anomalies over a rural reference zone rather than one WorldClim cell, retaining all three GCM values.
  5. Calibrate spatial parameters on a training subset of stations/days and report MAE, RMSE and correlation on held-out stations/days. Reject any calibration requiring negative UHI or failing to reproduce the urban–rural ordering.
  6. Use the completed temperature-only 2/3/5°C sensitivity to separate robust comparative conclusions from parameter-dependent magnitudes. Only after the observational gate, select the primary T_ref/UHI_max; then decide whether a new production run and downstream health/work-capacity recalculation are warranted. Do not mix outcomes generated under different UHI settings.

The diagnostic UCM runs were generated with run_ucm_scenarios.py under InVEST 3.20.2. The command omitted valuation flags, so only temperature outputs were produced.

The decimal-parameter test exposed and fixed an output-suffix issue in run_ucm_scenarios.py: decimal points are now encoded as p, without changing existing integer-run names.

Parameter tables and manifests are stored under the external data root:

1_preprocess/UrbanCoolingModel/OfficialWorkingInputs/climate/ucm_parameter_pilot_20261111_v2/

Baseline-only model outputs are stored separately from production:

2_postprocess_intermediate/UCM_official_runs/diagnostics/ucm_climate_parameter_pilot_20261111_v2/

The parameter folder contains station inventory, daily maxima, UHI distributions, GCM-specific anomalies, candidate parameters, station validation, London-mean comparisons, the 52-station acquisition screen and exact source hashes. Existing production outputs were not changed.

The expanded acquisition and analysis outputs are stored separately at:

1_preprocess/UrbanCoolingModel/OfficialWorkingInputs/climate/uhi_station_pilot_20261111_v1/

This folder contains the 60 source files, URL/hash acquisition manifest, completeness and daily-metric tables, primary and QC-sensitivity summaries, leave-one-station-out results, official MIDAS metadata snapshots, WorldCover exposure fractions, station-screening decisions, screened sensitivities and machine-readable analysis manifests.

The Crowd-Grid subset is stored under that folder at crowd_grid_recent_heat_packs_v1/. Its acquisition manifest records exact CEDA URLs, MD5 checksums and local SHA-256 hashes for 72 daily CSVs and the official MSOA boundary components. The folder also contains the station-to-MSOA lookup, 186-day contrast table and summary. Two initially downloaded Mole Valley CSVs are retained as unused provenance after the official boundary file placed Charlwood station in Crawley 001; the active manifest and analysis use Crawley.

The UHI sensitivity runs and machine-readable summaries are stored at:

2_postprocess_intermediate/UCM_official_runs/diagnostics/uhi_sensitivity_25c_20261111_v1/

The uhi2/ and uhi3/ subfolders contain separate scenario workspaces and run manifests. The summary/ subfolder contains London-wide, borough, spatial-range, rank-stability and Green–Target tables plus an analysis manifest with exact raster hashes. UHI 5°C values are read from the existing production run and are not copied or modified.

Before the daytime supplement was added, the station summary tables and manifests were copied in place with _pre_daytime_20261111 suffixes. This preserves the earlier daily-maximum/night-time-only result while the current tables add the daytime-mean sensitivity.

The v1 pilot is retained unchanged for comparison. The v2 manifests record the 2050 and 2070 inputs, five baseline-only UCM runs and generated-output hashes.

The interpretation of T_ref and UHI_max follows the InVEST Urban Cooling Model documentation. The proposed calibration and held-out validation gate follows the general evaluation principles in Hamel et al. (2024). London-specific context is provided by the six-year crowd-station study, summertime monitoring study, UKCP Local guidance and the historical London’s Warming technical report.
